page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8581C core with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 7.0 GB of system memory, yielding 3.5 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations reveal a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2081.0 and strong single-threaded compression performance, with gzip compression reaching 34.12 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show limitations. The multi-core stress-ng benchmark and Geekbench multi-core score of 2627.0 are categorized as weak, while uncached memory read and write bandwidths are poor, measuring 15.64 GB/sec and 10.0 GB/sec respectively.

From a resource density perspective, the c4-standard-2 offers an entry-level dedicated compute profile. While the inclusion of advanced CPU instruction sets like Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 provides hardware-level acceleration for specific cryptographic and integer operations, the overall system is constrained by its low memory capacity and weak memory bandwidth. This makes it a cost-efficient option for workloads that require dedicated CPU execution without high memory throughput or massive parallel processing demands.

This instance is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving. It can handle minor LLM text generation tasks for very small models (such as 135M parameters) at moderate speeds, but is poorly suited for larger model inference, database operations, or memory-intensive compilation tasks.
